newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols softer despite weak bonds.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols softer despite weak bonds.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. fixed-income options were steady to softer despite a late slide in underlying markets, dealers said.

March Treasury bond futures finished near the session low of 111-00, down about half a point on the day. But traders said sentiment was not as bearish as such a price movement suggested, blaming temporary indigestion of the Treasury's of $17.5 billion two-year note offering today for the losses.
"The auction looked like it went fairly well and the Beige Book didn't look like it carried any serious problems," said a Eurodollar trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME).

A T-bond trader at the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) said that despite the general weakness in volatilities, there was good buying in out-of-the-money calls, likely to be speculating on a rebound in bond prices.
He said several firms bought a total of 3,000-4,000 contracts in March 113 calls in CBOT T-bond futures options and that there was also interest in September 112 calls.
"People are taking shots with a lot of these cheap calls," he noted.
Implied volatility for March T-bond futures options was off some 0.2 point from Tuesday to around 9.7 percent.
Traders pointed out that volatilities for March options was becoming choppy as the contract approached its expiration on February 21.
They added that the fluctuations tended to be stronger on the downside as theta, the rate of time-decay, was getting steeper and weighed on premiums.

Implied volatility for June Eurodollar futures options was off 0.1-0.2 point to around 12.3 percent, while September was steady at about 15.2 percent. In early pit trading, a bank was said to have sold 2,000 contracts of June 93.75 puts and another firm was seen selling 3,000 of March 94.25 calls.

Traders saw little lasting effect on the market from the Treasury's two-year note auction and the Federal Reserve's Beige Book report, in which the central bank said it saw moderate growth and no big price pressures.
The Treasury's two-year note auction produced a high yield of 5.984 percent and a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.44 times.

The Beige Book -- coming on the heels of Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks Tuesday, which were perceived to be less hawkish than the market had feared -- aided a widespread view that the Fed's policy was on hold for now, traders said.
